note: Stories cluster the last 24 hours of collector items. Summaries come only from item titles and feed summaries; open the links before citing details.

stories.headline: Qatar's PM delivers Iran ceasefire proposal to Trump; 'positive momentum' reported
stories.summary: Qatar's prime minister met Trump and Vance at the White House and delivered a proposal built with Iran's two-day plan, covering nuclear issues, Hormuz and non-aggression. Trump spoke of positive momentum toward ending the war, though officials doubt an imminent deal. Qatari voices hint at good news soon, and a US-Iran round in Doha is reportedly being considered.
stories.turkey: A US-Iran settlement brokered via Doha would ease Türkiye's border, energy and trade exposure, but Ankara is a side-player to Qatari mediation.

stories.headline: Trump calls Iran war militarily over, says new strikes unlikely but forces ready
stories.summary: After meeting Qatar's prime minister, Trump said further military action against Iran does not seem necessary and the war is effectively over militarily. He said US forces remain ready, and that Qatar and Saudi Arabia want a peaceful deal. Iranian officials dismissed the claims as fake news and Iran's security chief denied talks with Washington.
stories.turkey: Reduced odds of renewed US strikes lower the risk of refugee flows, energy shocks and regional spillover on Türkiye's border.

stories.headline: Iran rejects Rubio's stance, insists blockade and sanctions end before talks
stories.summary: Iran's foreign ministry and security chiefs say negotiations are impossible under a naval blockade and war. They demand sanctions relief and seven conditions, while defending the two-day Hormuz proposal. Rubio called the conditions ridiculous and unrealistic, said progress is unproductive, and called the war unpopular but necessary. Tehran rejected moving enriched uranium abroad.
stories.turkey: Hardening positions reduce room for the Turkish-backed de-escalation track and prolong regional energy uncertainty.

stories.summary: Erdoğan said he conveyed Türkiye's concerns about possible new attacks on Iran to Trump and said Ankara does not want a new wave of strikes. He reportedly offered to facilitate an Iran-US settlement as Ankara and regional mediators push a seven-point de-escalation proposal.
stories.turkey: Ankara is positioning itself as a mediator to head off a regional escalation that would hit its economy and borders.

stories.headline: Syria weighs joining Saudi-Turkish-Pakistani defence pact amid troop deployment reports
stories.summary: Reports say Syria is preparing to join a defence pact with Türkiye, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan and to send about 600 fighters to Saudi Arabia near the Yemen border. Officials told the AP that Syrian military advisers are already in the kingdom. Foreign Minister al-Shaibani denied plans to send troops to Yemen, saying the Saudi military deal excludes this. Separately, Egypt's parliament approved a troop deployment requested by Riyadh.
stories.turkey: Syria's entry into a Türkiye-linked defence bloc would deepen Ankara's regional alliance network and its influence in Damascus.

stories.headline: Türkiye begins handing Bashiqa and Zilkan bases to Iraq, tied to Sinjar PKK exit
stories.summary: Ankara and Baghdad announced that Türkiye will start handing over its Bashiqa/Zilkan base near Mosul to Iraq in phases from November. Full withdrawal is expected by the end of 2026. The move is linked to ending the PKK presence in Sinjar under a joint committee.
stories.turkey: A drawdown from northern Iraq trades a forward military footprint for Baghdad's commitment to remove the PKK from Sinjar.

He said no concessions will be made in the funding crisis, and that Türkiye has committed 'not just its hand but its body'. Speaker Kurtulmuş linked domestic peace to a terror-free regional order.

The Paris prosecutor opened an inquiry into IRGC unit Shahid Kaveh, and France summoned Iran's ambassador. Paris seeks EU-level sanctions and international arrest warrants.
stories.turkey: Rising European-Iranian confrontation adds a hybrid-threat dimension that could complicate Ankara's balancing between Tehran and the West.
